verdict_reason: Explicit, legible text ties this pile to one site: an exhibit label reading 'GACH - Thuc dan Phap dung de xay dung nha tu Hoa Lo / Bricks used by French colonialists to build Hoa Lo prison, 1896', an introduction panel signed 'BAN QUAN LY DI TICH NHA TU HOA LO' about prisoners held 'in Hoa Lo prison from 1899 to 1954', a picture caption 'Hoa Lo political prisoners holding a meeting on the Labor Day (1 May 1932)', and the gate arch lettered 'MAISON CENTRALE' with the Hanoi Towers high-rise behind it. Everything else in the sheet is the same visit: cell blocks with black tarred dados, barred gates, the ankle-stock dioramas, the gilt memorial room, perimeter walls with spikes and razor wire, and framed archive exhibits. The two 3505* frames from a different uploader are the only ones without direct textual proof, and even they show a walled heritage courtyard with relief panels and a chained-off stone structure consistent with the site. The pin at 105.8465,21.0256 sits on Hoa Lo itself, so it is a real place, not a snapped centroid.
place_if_genuine: Hoa Lo Prison (Maison Centrale), 1 Hoa Lo, Hanoi

photos.place: Hoa Lo Prison (Maison Centrale), 1 Hoa Lo, Hanoi
photos.evidence: Narrow paved courtyard between a tall grey wall carrying framed stone/bronze relief panels of figures in conical hats and soldiers, and a low tile-roofed range with a row of dark doorways and a wooden bench. A leafless banyan/almond tree with red votive threads, and a beige stone-clad high-rise looming over the wall. Chained off at centre is a rough concreted stone structure with a dark arched opening and an interpretation plaque - consistent with the displayed escape sewer at Hoa Lo, and the high-rise with the Hanoi Towers block built on the demolished part of the prison. Read from site character, not from a legible sign.
